newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks up on plan, peso indifferent.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks up on plan, peso indifferent.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo's economic plan gave a boost to Mexican stocks but the peso was indifferent to the news, traders and analysts said on Tuesday.
"A lot of buying came in after the news, with a large amount from U.S. funds. Now we are seeing a healthy profit taking," said a trader from the stock market who declined to be named.
Zedillo's announcement of the National Program to Finance Development boosted stocks to a late morning high of 4,071.86 before falling to 4,056.15 points, largely on profit taking.
The benchmark 48-hour peso moved little during the day at 7.9130 to 7.9160 per dollar in early afternoon trading..
"The news did not affect the (foreign exchange) market significantly. It's been quiet," said a peso trader who declined to be named.
Earlier in the day Zedillo unveiled a plan that targets economic growth of an average five percent annually through 2000 and seeks to boost domestic savings.
"I liked the part about the GDP growth, which seems extraordinary. The exports support should mean that they will let the exchange rate slip," the stock market trader said.
Traders said stocks surged on estimates of growth and May inflation of less than 1.08 percent.

"The president and (Finance Minister Guillermo) Ortiz's announcements are influencing stocks a lot. The market broke its historic record with considerable strength," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Joaquin Vaca said.
One trader said the markets would take some time to evaluate the estimates.
